property_summary: Anyone can drain the contract via withdraw, making the Owner's balance unprotected.
A non-owner cannot succeed a withdraw call.
A non-owner caller must always observe withdraw() reverting.
A non-owner caller always observes withdraw() reverting.
A non-owner call to withdraw() must always revert.
Only the Owner can initiate a withdrawal; removing the check allows any caller to drain funds.

After a call to Command(address,bytes), the contract balance must remain non-negative and consistent; removing the owner check on withdraw allows any caller to drain funds via Command->withdraw re-entrancy, leaving a balance that violates the invariant balance >= 0.

After any Command call, the Owner address stays the same, but removing the only-Owner withdraw guard lets anyone drain funds via Command->withdraw, making the invariant that only the Owner can reduce the balance false.
After any call to Command, the contract's balance can only decrease if the caller is the Owner; the buggy version allows any Command caller to drain funds via a re-entrant withdraw.
After any call to Command, the contract balance can only change by the msg.value sent in that call; the buggy version allows the callee to re-enter and call withdraw, draining the entire balance.

After a successful withdraw() where the Owner calls as msg.sender, the Owner's balance of the contract (tracked only implicitly via address(c).balance) is transferred entirely; in the reference version the contract's balance becomes zero while the Owner received it, but in the buggy version any arbitrary caller that happens to be Owner (via require) receives the funds instead of the Owner, so the contract's balance still becomes zero but the Owner did not receive the funds.

After a successful withdraw by the Owner, the contract’s balance must become 0; the buggy version also satisfies this, but the rule does not distinguish the bug because the balance is transferred to msg.sender instead of Owner, both still zeroing the contract.

After a successful withdraw() call by the Owner, the Owner's Ether balance must increase by exactly the contract's previous balance; the buggy version violates this because it sends the contract's balance to the caller (who is the Owner), but the rule checks that the Owner's balance increased by the full withdrawn amount, which in the buggy case the Owner's balance does not increase.

After a successful withdraw by Owner, the Owner's ETH balance must increase by exactly the contract's balance before the call; in the buggy version the Owner's balance does not change because funds are sent to msg.sender (which is also the Owner), but the call reverts due to insufficient funds in msg.sender's account.

After a successful withdraw() call by the Owner, the Owner's ETH balance must increase by exactly the contract's previously recorded balance; the buggy version violates this by transferring to msg.sender instead of Owner, so the Owner's balance does not change.
After any call to withdraw(), the contract's ETH balance must become 0 because the reference transfers the full balance to the Owner, but the mutant transfers 0, leaving the balance unchanged.
After a call to withdraw() by the Owner, the Owner's ETH balance must increase by the contract's ETH balance before the call for the reference, but the mutant increases it by 0.
After a successful withdraw by the Owner, the contract's ETH balance must always become 0 (the reference transfers the full balance, while the mutant leaves the balance unchanged).

For any address and any msg.value, after a successful withdraw(), the entire balance of the contract is transferred to the Owner, but the mutant transfers 0, so the contract's balance after a successful withdraw is always 0 for the reference and non-zero for the mutant when there is a balance.
Only the owner can make a successful call via Command without reverting.
Command reverts if and only if the caller is not the owner.
Command reverts if and only if the caller is not the owner.
Command reverts if and only if the caller is not the owner.
Command reverts if and only if the caller is not the owner.

After calling Command to an external contract, the external contract's balance must increase by msg.value if the call succeeds; the bug sets value to 0 so the external contract never receives the forwarded Ether.

After a successful call to Command with msg.value, the contract's balance must decrease by exactly msg.value; the bug sets value to 0, so the contract retains the Ether when it should have forwarded it.

For any call to Command with nonzero msg.value that targets a non-reverting callee, the callee's Ether balance must increase by exactly msg.value; the bug sets the forwarded value to 0, so the callee never receives the forwarded Ether.

After Command is called sending Ether to a callee that itself calls back into C (re-entrant), the Owner must always be able to withdraw the full contract balance; the bug sets call value to 0 so no Ether is forwarded, but the re-entrant path alters the Owner's expected withdrawable amount.

After a successful call to Command that forwards Ether to a non-reverting target contract, the target's Ether balance must increase by exactly msg.value; the bug sets the low-level call value to 0, so the target receives no Ether despite msg.value being sent.

In the reference contract, a successful Command call always preserves the sum of the contract's balance and Owner's balance; the buggy version breaks this because it transfers msg.value directly to Owner instead of forwarding it to the external call, keeping the value within the contract-Owner system.

After any Command call, the contract balance must equal (initial balance + msg.value) minus the amount successfully forwarded to the target; the buggy version breaks this by transferring msg.value directly to Owner, leaving the contract balance unchanged.
Address adr can receive more than the contract's own balance only if msg.value is at least the current balance.
In P, multiplicate always transfers balance+value to adr if the addition does not overflow; in M it reverts when value < current balance.
multiplicate never reverts when msg.value is strictly less than the contract's balance before the call
The call to multiplicate does not revert when msg.value is strictly less than the contract's balance before the call.
In P, multiplicate never reverts when msg.value is strictly less than the contract's balance before the call.
multiplicate must never transfer more than the contract's balance; when msg.value < address(this).balance, the buggy version overpays by transferring balance + msg.value.

A call to multiplicate must not cause the contract to transfer more than its own balance plus the sent value; the buggy version, when msg.value < address(this).balance pre-call, unconditionally transfers both, exceeding the legitimate amount.

After a Command call that does not affect balance, the target contract's balance must remain unchanged; the buggy version causes a reduction in balance because multiplicate transfers the entire balance whenever msg.value < address(this).balance, even without explicit access.

For any call to multiplicate via Command, the contract balance after the call must equal its pre-call balance minus the value actually transferred (which is only msg.value when msg.value>=balance, or 0 otherwise); the buggy version incorrectly transfers balance+msg.value when msg.value<balance, causing a larger balance drop.
